source_note: Oxford Podcasts series page https://podcasts.ox.ac.uk/series/romp-through-ethics-complete-beginners plus each individual episode page (parts 1-7 and 'Further reading and more...'); fetched 2026-10-21.

lectures.title: Rules, truths and theories: an introduction to ethical reasoning
lectures.summary: Introduces ethical reasoning by examining moral dilemmas, moral truth and moral knowledge, and freewill and determinism.

lectures.title: Freedom, knowledge and society: the preconditions of ethical reasoning
lectures.summary: Examines the preconditions of ethical reasoning and makes a comparison between the law of the land and the moral law.

lectures.title: Virtue Ethics: virtue, values and character
lectures.summary: Reflects on Aristotle's account of morality and the centrality of the virtues within it.

lectures.title: Humean Ethics: Non-Cognitivism, the passions and moral motivation
lectures.summary: Reflects on Hume's account of morality and his rejection of reason as the source of morality, covering non-cognitivism, the passions and moral motivation.

lectures.title: Deontology: Kant, duty and the moral law
lectures.summary: Reflects on Kant's account of morality, including the categorical imperative.

lectures.title: Utilitarianism: Mill and the utility calculus
lectures.summary: Reflects on Mill's account of morality and the greatest happiness of the greatest number, together with the utility calculus.

lectures.title: Making Up Your Mind
lectures.summary: The final episode takes stock and brings together all the strands considered across the series.

lectures.title: Further reading and more...
lectures.summary: A closing resource item telling listeners who have finished the series where to go from here.
